candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001]! I’m preparing a response to an RFQ that is separate from the Tpec project. It appears fairly straightforward and will involve combining all content into one document, creating the layout, org. chart, and budget sheet, and handling the formatting. The response deadline is 7/31, although I plan to submit it on 7/30. Would you be interested in assisting me with this? If yes, could you quote the total cost? I’ll also send the RFQ shortly for your reference. Thanks!

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: That estimate seems reasonable. Because this is an RFQ rather than an RFP, I expect it could be somewhat shorter—perhaps no more than 20 pages.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Unfortunately, that exceeds my budget and seems broader in scope than I need. Could we develop a more straightforward option? I’m envisioning one formatting/layout pass on the final draft using GreenLatinos' existing brand colors and fonts, one revision round, and delivery as a print-ready PDF. More specifically, I think I need 1) layout and graphic treatment for the entire document and 2) incorporation of tables/photos/org chart/graphics into the final draft. I’m also assuming an RFP could potentially follow later, since the RFQ is typically the first step. What would this revised option cost?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Thank you for providing the $1400.00 estimate. That works for me.

A few items:

1) My subcontractors won’t send me their content until EOD next Wednesday, so your working period will be compressed. Would you be able to turn it around within 48-hour of receiving the final narrative content from me, followed by a 24-hour turnaround on your end for the final revisions?

2) For the branding, I’ve shifted the focus from the client’s brand to the bidder’s brand—mine! I’d like the design to reflect my company, Agua Arc. I can provide my logo and colors.

3) Because this will be the first proposal I’m submitting as a prime, and I launched my company less than a year ago and work solo, I’d like to use this proposal as a template going forward. Ideally, the template you build would have modular/swappable sections so future proposals don’t need to be recreated from the beginning. In particular, I’m imagining a) a flexible narrative-section framework, since some proposals may have 5 sections v 8 sections, b) a modular table design that can be resized for different budget structures, and c) a “prepared for \_\_\_ \[client name\]” credit line instead of client branding.

4) Regarding Canva, can I own the files without having a paid subscription? Would there be any other source files, or would everything exist solely in Canva?

Thank you!

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 3) That makes sense. For now, let’s keep this first proposal straightforward and return to the template later. Could you confirm that I’ll still be able to edit it in Canva? I want that option in case I need to make any last-minute changes after your final review.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Everything you described sounds good! I really appreciate your flexibility!

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Hi! Thank you—I’m attaching the skeleton now. Please keep two things in mind: 1) the section sequence was established by the client's Q&A, which was released Friday night, and it cannot be redesigned, so we must retain the order shown in this skeleton; and 2) the final deliverable will be one PDF submitted via email, so the template needs to support a clean PDF export that is "emailable" (I’m not sure whether I previously mentioned that). Thank you!

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 1) This folder contains photos for inclusion in the document. The images I definitely want included are marked with asterisks in their titles. [URL_003]

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 2) The proposal contains many hyperlinks, and it’s essential that all of them remain functional. I’m noting this to ensure the links still work after the final file is saved. Thank you!

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 3) One additional note: please ensure the fonts are uniform, using the same typefaces in the relevant sections and the correct sizes.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: The document appears lengthy, though I think much of that is due to the spacing. Hopefully, you can bring it within the page limit; please let me know if that isn’t possible.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Hi! One of the contractors unexpectedly sent me 4 additional resumes for the proposal. I hadn’t anticipated having more team members, so I now need to prepare 4 more bios for the Appendix under Message Agency. Could you add a placeholder for each of these 4 bios so I can insert them during my review? Thanks.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: [FREELANCER_NAME_001], I need to swap out two of the proposal’s tables, and I’m sorry for the change. The replacements are in this document. Hopefully, you haven’t reached that portion of the layout yet; if you have, I hope replacing the two tables won’t create too much inconvenience. Thank you. [URL_005]

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: I also added the new bios to the Tables doc, in case you’re able to insert them directly instead of using placeholders. Thank you!!

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Good morning!

That approach works for me. Thank you.

I hadn’t expected the document to become this long, but I’m hoping we can decrease the spacing between sections and paragraphs to move it closer to the original page limit.

During my review, I’m also hoping to shorten the letter \(first page\) so it fits on one page.

If any other portions feel awkward, I can try trimming the content further when I review it, if that would help.

Thank you for collaborating with me on this and continuing to share progress updates.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 1) For the cover/TOC/Page Divider for Appendix and Last Page, I’m not very fond of the light pink/cream background wash on those pages. Is there another approach you could try? Otherwise, I think we should perhaps use white, consistent with the remainder of the document.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 2) The letter will be one page, and I also need to insert my signature. I’m hoping I can handle that easily in Canva. However, the two pictures currently placed on the letter’s second page are two of my favorites for this proposal, so if they won’t fit in the one-page letter, I hope you can relocate them to another section.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 3) On Page 15, could the tree be made more prominent in the picture? Perhaps by zooming out?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 4) On Page 19, please delete the picture of the boy wearing a white t-shirt in front of the garden. You can either substitute a different photo or leave the page with only one picture.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 5) For Page 24, can the picture with the lady show more of the tree?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: 6) On Page 30, could we also display the entire tree in this photo?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Good morning! I’m still making the edits directly in Canva. I wanted to alert you that I just discovered the master doc I sent you was missing a subsection from Section 2. I flagged this in the Canva comments, but I’m also providing it here so you can quickly access the content that must be added. My apologies for not catching this sooner. [URL_005]

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: [FREELANCER_NAME_001] - Unfortunately, it became necessary to add two rows per phase to the Payment and Milestone Schedule table. I placed the updated table in the Google doc that was shared earlier today. I’m unsure whether it will be simpler for you to add two rows per phase for the new additions or replace the entire table. When you reach this revision, please let me know if you have any questions. Thanks.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: [FREELANCER_NAME_001] - I’m fitting in a little reviewing between meetings and will note anything incorrect here. 1) The tree is no longer visible enough in the photo on page 11. I’m hoping you can zoom out slightly so a bit more of the tree can be seen again. Thanks.
